title: Roles Oncall Simulator & Access Review Walkthrough
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: Admins and SREs need a low-risk way to validate role changes and access reviews across orgs and workspaces before rolling them out. Current console screens list roles and permissions but do not make it easy to simulate oncall rotations, escalation windows, or transient grants.

Goal: Ship a compact interactive walkthrough in the Console that lets operators: (1) simulate a user or service identity and step through effective permissions across nested role inheritance, (2) run a time-bounded "oncall escalation" scenario to preview what audit logs and alerts would look like, and (3) produce an 'Audit Delta' snapshot (CSV + human summary) for compliance reviewers. The flow should be usable in both Hosted and Private deployments and respect KMS/PII redaction rules.

Proposed UX: A three-pane modal that surfaces (A) Identity selector + timeline controls, (B) Role inheritance visualizer with collapsible grants, and (C) Log & cost preview that estimates whether escalation actions would hit Dedicated capacity or increase token/compute cost. Prototype includes keyboard-first navigation, colorblind-safe palettes, and a compact CSV export action.

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- We will show only policy-level statements and not raw KMS keys or HSM identifiers to avoid leaking sensitive config.
- Timeline simulation uses sampled audit events and synthetic "what-if" events to avoid running costly live queries; trade-off is potential false positives for very recent custom grants.
- Role inheritance visualizer will flatten cross-workspace role mappings for readability; full graph mode is available behind an "Advanced" toggle to prevent cognitive overload.
- Accessibility: ensure screen-reader order and ARIA labels for virtualized lists.

Deliverables: Figma prototype (interactive modal + full-screen dive), annotated flow doc in Confluence, acceptance criteria and QA checklist.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Initial concept sketch posted to Figma. Shared with PM and Eng for feasibility review. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/console-rbac-simulators

2026-02-25 - Engineering raised performance questions around live audit sampling (ENG-1984). We agreed to use sampled events and modeled synthetic events for the timeline; ENG will provide a paginated API to fetch event buckets.

2026-03-01 - Design critique with Security and Legal: remove direct KMS identifiers, add redaction toggle and mandatory 'reason' field when exporting Audit Delta. Legal asked for an audit retention note in the export header.

2026-03-04 - Usability test (n=6) with platform engineers: participants completed role simulation tasks faster with the collapsible inheritance view; some confusion around 'temporary grant' UX. Action: change wording to 'Transient Grant (expires)'.
2026-03-08 - PM requested adding cost estimate per action to help SREs decide whether to escalate via Automation or use runbook. UX added a small cost-sparkline beside expensive actions.
2026-03-10 - Submitted for design review. Attached prototype and acceptance criteria. Feedback requested by 2026-03-12.
acceptance_criteria: Given an identity, the simulator shows effective permissions across workspace and org roles within 3s for the sample dataset
The timeline "oncall escalation" playback exports an Audit Delta CSV and a human-readable summary that includes redaction metadata
Advanced graph mode shows full role relationship graph (interactive, pan/zoom) and is reachable from the modal
Exported CSV strips KMS/HSM identifiers and includes a redaction flag per row
Cost preview annotates actions with dedicated/dynamic cost tags and an estimated per-minute cost
Keyboard navigation and screen reader labels are implemented for core modal controls
review_notes: Security: Approved concept pending export redaction enforcement. See comment thread on Confluence page for legal wording.
Eng (Serving Runtime): Needs an API endpoint to return 'estimated cost per action' and a flag for Dedicated capacity impact (ENG-2010).
PM: Prioritize CSV export and 'simulate user' entrypoint for Cycle 41; defer runbook templating to later cycle.
Design QA: Check virtualization edge cases when >2,000 role edges are present; provide graceful collapse point at 500 edges.
next_steps: Incorporate security review wording into export header and update spec by 2026-03-12
Hand off annotated Figma to ENG with component tokens and accessibility notes (deadline 2026-03-16)
Create a small e2e test harness for the simulator UI using synthetic audit buckets (ENG-1984), link PR once available
Prepare release notes copy and short help center article draft for Console release 2026.03
